items.statement: Across reviews, after correcting for overlap, a normal point-of-care lactate at triage leaves at least one in twenty adults with suspected sepsis falsely reassured, so it cannot justify lowering priority.
items.rationale: The retrieved pooled figure (c2) exceeds this bound; the umbrella review tests whether it holds across non-overlapping evidence of adequate confidence.
items.risks: Few reviews report negative predictive value directly.

items.statement: A threshold of 4 mmol/L gives few false alarms but misses most patients with sepsis, so no single threshold serves both escalation and reassurance.
items.rationale: Follows the threshold trade-off in the pooled accuracy review (c1 and its 4 mmol/L figures).

items.statement: Reviews that reach opposite conclusions share most of their primary studies and differ mainly in outcome definitions.
items.rationale: Suggested by the overlap assessment (c3); explains the disagreement the investigator sees.

summary: h1 selected as the proposition most relevant to the triage rule.
